flags.note: The premise of the flag is factually wrong about the draft. Slide 8 discloses the conflict the flag says is missing, in the disclosure block directly beneath the quote: the Brennholt Family Office 'holds a non-voting minority interest in the Investment Manager, so it benefits financially when the Fund raises new capital.' The same block also gives current-client status ('current investor in the Fund'), compensation status ('received no cash or non-cash compensation'), and the reduced-fee Founders Class conflict. All C1 elements are present and adjacent to the testimonial, so it is clear and prominent. Nothing here for a reviewer to work on.

C3 is limited on its face to performance of a portfolio 'other than a private fund.' This is a private fund: Slide 1 restricts it to accredited investors who are also qualified purchasers, and Slide 2 states any offer will be made only by the PPM. The 1-, 5- and 10-year presentation requirement is therefore not triggered. Separately, Slide 5 already gives every calendar year from 2017 inception through 2025 plus 2026 YTD and a since-inception annualized figure, so an investor can derive the standard periods. Misapplication of the code.

Genuine C4 concern worth a reviewer's time. Slide 6 carves out an explicitly self-identified best twelve months (April 1, 2020 - March 31, 2021, 41.8% net) from a nine-and-a-half-year record that elsewhere shows 1.7% (2022), 3.1% (2018) and a -12.6% peak-to-trough decline. Labelling the window 'our best' does not cure it; selecting a peak sub-period out of a longer available record and placing it on the forward-looking opportunity-set slide is exactly the unfair period selection C4 addresses. Not one of the listed known issues.

Genuine C7 concern. Slide 3's 'Ranked the No. 1 event-driven fund by Brisenden Okehurst Research, ahead of more than 140 peer funds' identifies the provider but omits the date the rating was given, the period it covers, and whether the Fund or Investment Manager paid compensation for it - three of the four required elements. The claim is prominent on the firm-credentials slide and also invites a C6 substantiation question. Not one of the listed known issues.
